    - StaticText "01 — WHAT IS KIMI K2"
    - heading "The Open-Source Model That Changed the Frontier" [level=2, ref=e10]
    - paragraph
      - StaticText "Kimi K2 is Moonshot AI's "
      - strong
        - StaticText "state-of-the-art Mixture-of-Experts language model"
      - StaticText ", released in July 2025 under a Modified MIT License. With one trillion total parameters and 32 billion activated per token, it became the most capable open-source agentic model available at release — distinguished not by scale alone, but by Moonshot's deliberate focus on autonomous, tool-using workflows over static benchmark performance."
    - paragraph
      - StaticText "What made K2's release historically significant was a rare combination: "
      - strong
        - StaticText "frontier benchmark performance"
      - StaticText " across coding, reasoning, and knowledge tasks; "
      - strong
        - StaticText "deep native tool-use capability"
      - StaticText " built through post-training on synthetic agentic scenarios; and "
      - strong
        - StaticText "full commercially usable open weights"
      - StaticText ". Prior to K2, models at this capability level existed exclusively behind closed vendor APIs. K2 made frontier-class agentic intelligence genuinely accessible."
    - paragraph
      - StaticText "K2 ships in two variants: "
      - strong
        - StaticText "K2-Base"
      - StaticText " - the raw pre-trained model for researchers and builders who want fine-tuning control; and "
      - strong
        - StaticText "K2-Instruct"
      - StaticText " — the post-trained model ready for conversational and agentic use out of the box. Both sets of weights are on HuggingFace in block-fp8 format."

    - generic
      - StaticText "02 — MOE ARCHITECTURE"
      - heading "Mixture-of-Experts: Why 32B Active Feels Like 1T" [level=2, ref=e18]
      - paragraph
        - StaticText "Kimi K2's Mixture-of-Experts architecture is the engineering foundation that makes the model simultaneously powerful and practical to deploy. Rather than activating all one trillion parameters for every token — which would make inference cost-prohibitive — K2 uses "
        - strong
          - StaticText "sparse activation"
        - StaticText ": only 32 billion parameters engage for any given token."
      - paragraph
        - StaticText "The architecture contains "
        - strong
          - StaticText "384 specialized expert networks"
        - StaticText " organized across 61 layers: one dense standardization layer at the base followed by 60 MoE layers for hierarchical processing. For each token, K2's routing mechanism selects exactly "
        - strong
          - StaticText "8 specialist experts plus one shared expert"
        - StaticText ". The shared expert ensures universal knowledge access; the 8 selected experts bring task-specific capabilities. This fine-grained routing — 384 experts with 9 activated — provides more specialization depth than coarser designs (e.g., 8 total experts with 2 activated)."
      - paragraph
        - StaticText "The practical result: K2 delivers the knowledge capacity and representational depth of a trillion-parameter system at the "
        - strong
          - StaticText "inference cost of a ~32B dense model"
        - StaticText ". API token costs are dramatically lower than the headline parameter count suggests, and self-hosted deployments need far less GPU memory than a truly dense 1T model would require. K2's MoE architecture is comparable in principle to DeepSeek-V3 but distinct in routing granularity, expert dimensionality, and the MuonClip optimizer that stabilizes training at this scale."
      - list
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
          - StaticText "— 64 attention heads via Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA)"
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
            - StaticText "Expert intermediate dimension: 2,048"
          - StaticText "— per MoE expert network"
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
          - StaticText "— proven performance at large model scale"
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
          - StaticText "— broad multilingual, code, and scientific coverage"
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
          - StaticText "— efficient storage and inference"
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
          - StaticText "— reduces KV cache size at longer context lengths"

    - generic
      - StaticText "03 — MUONCLIP OPTIMIZER"
      - heading "MuonClip: Stable Training at Unprecedented Scale" [level=2, ref=e19]
      - paragraph
        - StaticText "Training a 1T-parameter MoE model is a genuinely hard engineering challenge. MoE architectures at this scale are prone to "
        - strong
          - StaticText "attention logit explosion"
        - StaticText " — where values in the attention layers grow unbounded during training, causing catastrophic loss spikes and requiring expensive checkpoint rollbacks. Historically, training runs at this scale have required multiple interventions to recover from instability events."
      - paragraph
        - StaticText "Moonshot AI developed "
        - strong
          - StaticText "MuonClip"
        - StaticText " specifically to solve this problem. MuonClip applies the Muon optimizer — an improvement over standard Adam that applies the Nesterov momentum update in the spectral domain for better gradient conditioning — at unprecedented trillion-parameter scale. The key innovation is a novel "
        - strong
          - StaticText "qk-clip technique"
        - StaticText ": rather than using standard gradient clipping after the fact, MuonClip directly adjusts the query and key projection matrices in the attention mechanism to prevent logit explosion before it begins."
      - paragraph
        - StaticText "The outcome was a complete pre-training run of 1 trillion parameters on "
        - strong
          - StaticText "15.5 trillion tokens with zero training instability"
        - StaticText ". This is an unusual achievement — most large MoE training runs encounter instability events requiring restart from checkpoint. Moonshot's ability to complete a clean 15.5T token run at this scale is a significant engineering validation of MuonClip's design, and it carries forward to K2.5 and K2.6 with the same stability characteristics."
      - list
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
          - StaticText "— Nesterov momentum in the spectral domain, superior gradient conditioning vs Adam"
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
          - StaticText "— proactively prevents attention logit explosion in MoE layers"
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
          - StaticText "— clean run across all 15.5T tokens, no loss spike interventions"
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
          - StaticText "— unprecedented use of Muon-family optimizers"
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
          - StaticText "— MuonClip is consistent from K2 to K2.6"
      - generic

    - generic
      - StaticText "04 — K2 THINKING · NOV 2025"
      - heading "K2 Thinking: Where Reasoning Meets Tool Use" [level=2, ref=e20]
      - paragraph
        - StaticText "Kimi K2 Thinking is the post-trained reasoning variant released in "
        - strong
          - StaticText "November 2025"
        - StaticText ", four months after the original K2. It introduced a capability that had not been achieved reliably at production scale before: "
        - strong
          - StaticText "seamlessly interleaved chain-of-thought reasoning with native tool calls"
        - StaticText "."
      - paragraph
        - StaticText "In practice, this means K2 Thinking can reason about a problem, determine that it needs external data or a code execution result, call the appropriate tool, receive the result, reason about the result, decide on a follow-up action, call another tool, and continue this reasoning-action chain for "
        - strong
          - StaticText "up to 200–300 sequential steps"
        - StaticText " without losing track of the overall task. Earlier reasoning models would either complete their full thinking trace before acting, or execute tool calls without integrated reasoning between them — not both simultaneously."
      - paragraph
        - StaticText "K2 Thinking also introduced "
        - strong
          - StaticText "Quantization-Aware Training (QAT)"
        - StaticText " at the post-training stage. By incorporating INT4 weight-only quantization to MoE components during training — rather than applying it as post-hoc compression — K2 Thinking achieves a "
        - strong
          - StaticText "~2× generation speed improvement"
        - StaticText " over FP16 inference without accuracy degradation. All K2 Thinking benchmark results are measured under INT4 precision, making them directly comparable to production deployment characteristics."
      - list
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
          - StaticText "— reason, act, observe, reason, act — seamlessly"
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
          - StaticText "— without losing task coherence"
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
          - StaticText "— ~2× speed vs FP16, no accuracy degradation"
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
            - StaticText "Recommended temperature: 1.0"
          - StaticText "— for optimal reasoning chain quality"
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
          - StaticText "— access full chain-of-thought trace for debugging"
        - listitem [level=1]
          - StaticText "→"
          - strong
            - StaticText "Partners: Tencent CodeBuddy, Genspark"
          - StaticText "— production deployments built on K2 Thinking"
      - StaticText "API ACCESS"
      - paragraph
        - StaticText "K2 Thinking API: "
        - code
          - StaticText "platform.moonshot.ai"
        - StaticText ", model: "
        - code

        - StaticText ". Recommended "
        - code

      - heading "Python API Quick Start" [level=3, ref=e24]
      - StaticText "Python · OpenAI SDK · K2 Instruct & K2 Thinking"
      - generic
        - StaticText "# pip install openai from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI( api_key=\"YOUR_MOONSHOT_API_KEY\", # get at platform.moonshot.ai base_url=\"https://api.moonshot.ai/v1\" ) # K2 Instruct — conversational & agentic (temperature 0.6) response = client.chat.completions.create( model=\"kimi-k2-instruct\", temperature=0.6, max_tokens=4096, messages=[ {\"role\": \"system\", \"content\": \"You are Kimi, an AI assistant by Moonshot AI.\"}, {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Debug this function and explain the fix...\"} ] ) print(response.choices[0].message.content) # K2 Thinking — extended chain-of-thought (temperature 1.0) thinking = client.chat.completions.create( model=\"kimi-k2-thinking\", temperature=1.0, messages=[{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Prove this algorithm is O(n log n)...\"}] ) # Access the chain-of-thought reasoning trace print(thinking.choices[0].message.reasoning_content) print(thinking.choices[0].message.content)"

      - StaticText "09 — K2 MODEL FAMILY"
      - heading "The Kimi K2 Family: 9 Months of Evolution" [level=2, ref=e34]
      - paragraph
        - StaticText "Between July 2025 and April 2026, Moonshot AI shipped five major model updates in the K2 lineage. This cadence — a major update roughly every two months — is faster than any closed-source frontier lab over the same period."
      - generic
        - StaticText "K2"

      - heading "Getting the Most from Kimi K2" [level=2, ref=e36]

      - heading "Use the Anthropic-compatible endpoint for Claude migrations" [level=4, ref=e40]
      - paragraph
        - StaticText "If migrating from Claude, use K2's Anthropic-compatible endpoint at platform.moonshot.ai. Note: the Anthropic API applies temperature scaling — "
      - StaticText "5"
      - heading "Validate self-hosted deployments before serving production" [level=4, ref=e41]
      - paragraph
      - StaticText "6"
      - heading "For new projects requiring vision or longer context, start with K2.5 or K2.6" [level=4, ref=e42]
      - paragraph
        - StaticText "K2 remains a solid cost-efficient model for text-only workflows. For new projects: if you need native image/video understanding, use K2.5 (256K context, MoonViT encoder). If you need Agent Swarm or the best possible long-horizon coding reliability, use K2.6 (262K, 300 agents, GA stability). Switching between K2 variants is a one-line model string change in your API calls."

For almost every team, this threshold is irrelevant. The weights are free to download and deploy."

        - StaticText "K2 (July 2025): text-only, 128K context, 65.8% SWE-bench. K2.5 (January 2026): added native vision (MoonViT encoder), 256K context, Agent Swarm (100 agents, 4.5× speedup), 76.8% SWE-bench. K2.6 (April 2026): 262K context, Agent Swarm 300 agents/4,000 steps, 80.2% SWE-bench, General Availability. K2 remains a strong cost-efficient model for text-only workflows where K2.5/K2.6 capabilities are not needed."

Enterprise-grade GPUs (A100-class minimum) are required for practical inference throughput. Before routing production traffic, run the official Kimi Vendor Verifier to confirm your deployment matches the reference implementation output characteristics."
